content: 1. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the effectiveness of insulin glargine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution is advised, and glycemic control should be closely monitored in diabetic patients. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. 2. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin glulisine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. 3. Levonorgestrel (oral) reduces the effects of inhaled insulin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution is advised, and glycemic control should be monitored. Ethinyl estradiol also decreases the effects of inhaled insulin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. 4. Estrogens, including ethinyl estradiol, may impair glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control closely in diabetic patients. 5. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the effects of insulin lispro through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. 6. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin NPH via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution is advised, and glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. 7. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the effects of regular human insulin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. 8. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is significant, and alternative therapies should be considered. Isavuconazonium sulfate also increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel (oral) and ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. 9. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel (oral) and ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. At a dose of 40 mg/day, istradefylline increased the peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials, but this effect was not observed at 20 mg/day. 10. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as itraconazole, may elevate plasma hormone levels. 11. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel (oral) and ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of these drugs. 12. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole, may elevate plasma hormone levels. 13. Levonorgestrel (oral) decreases the levels or effects of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Ethinyl estradiol also reduces lamotrigine levels through enhanced hepatic clearance. Combination oral contraceptives significantly decrease plasma concentrations of lamotrigine, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. 14. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 15. Larotrectinib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel (oral) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 16. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended when coadministered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage adjustments. 17. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel (oral) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrate levels for up to 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 18. Leniolisib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol through mechanisms involving BCRP inhibition. Alternative therapies should be considered, as leniolisib may increase systemic exposure to BCRP substrates. 19. Lesinurad decreases the effects of levonorgestrel (oral) and ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered, and additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Hormonal contraception alone should not be relied upon when taking lesinurad. 20. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the effects of letrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Concurrent use of letrozole with estrogens or estrogen-containing products should be avoided. 21. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. 22. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel (oral) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 23. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of liraglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Glycemic control should be closely monitored in diabetic patients. 24. Lixisenatide decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by delaying gastrointestinal absorption. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least 1 hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. 25. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. 26. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lonafarnib dose to the starting level and monitor for arrhythmias and other cardiac events. 27. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the levels or effects of lonapegsomatropin by reducing serum IGF-1 response to growth hormone analogs. A higher growth hormone dose may be required. 28. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 29. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel (oral) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered. 30. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unspecified mechanism. Hormonal contraceptives are not a reliable method of birth control when coadministered with lumacaftor/ivacaftor. 31. Lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 32. Levonorgestrel (oral) increases the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may increase the risk of toxicity. 33. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel (oral) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during coadministration and for 4 months after the last mavacamten dose. 34. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Glycemic control should be closely monitored in diabetic patients. 35. Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. 36. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of metyrapone through an unspecified mechanism. Discontinuation of estrogens, including oral contraceptives, may be advisable prior to and during metyrapone administration. 37. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 38. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of midazolam by inhibiting its metabolism. This interaction may prolong sedation. 39. Mifepristone decreases the effects of levonorgestrel (oral) and ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Alternative therapies should be considered. 40. Mineral oil decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. 41. Minocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. 42. Mitotane decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel (oral) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4, and dosage adjustments may be necessary when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates. 43. Momelotinib increases the toxicity of ethinyl estradiol by competing for plasma protein binding. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended.
